doc.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: John Hammond, Cal Lampley and Teo Macero
summary: He had no dealings with Hammond; his sessions with Cal Lampley helped break Teo Macero into jazz production.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: At Columbia – when I think of Columbia during that period, I know one of the influential people there is John Hammond. Hammond was an admirer of your music, but I don’t often hear his name in association with your time at Columbia. Did you have any dealings with John when you were at Columbia?
No, and I kept thinking I would have. But it was different artists represented the guys that – Cal Lampley. Do you remember that name? The first jazz that Teo [Macero]
ever did was, I believe, with me. So, in a way, I broke him into the business. He’s such a sharp guy. He caught on quite quickly.
